136	### 2. `restore_after`: the DAG, its order, its limits
137	
138	**2.1 Meaning.** `BlockDescriptor.restore_after` (ADR-0003 § 2) lists the blocks that must be **restored and post-restored before this one, and initialised (`default_state`, `init_world`) before this one**. One relation orders all four callables. A block may list a non-persisted block; a `WORLD` block listing a `PROFILE` block is legal and the edge is simply not visited by an in-session pass.
139	
140	**2.2 Compilation at the freeze.** In the registry validation pass (ADR-0003 § 8, after the hook schedule) the kernel builds the `RestorePlan`:
141	
142	1. Resolve every id to the block's **registration index**; an unregistered id is `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY` (code 10, existing). A duplicate entry in one list is dropped with a boot warning `RESTORE_AFTER_DUPLICATE` (warnings must be empty at the end of every CI run, as for hooks).
143	2. Run Kahn's algorithm over registration indices. **The ready list is ordered by registration index and the smallest ready index is always taken**, exactly the rule of the hook sort (ADR-0003 § 8), so there is one algorithm and a total order that is a pure function of registration data. Dictionary iteration never decides anything.
144	3. If unprocessed blocks remain with no ready block (this includes a block listing itself), boot fails with `RESTORE_CYCLE` (**new code**) naming the remaining blocks in registration order.
145	4. Record `order` (block indices in restore order) and `rank` (position per index), and derive three views: `world_order` (persisted `WORLD` blocks), `post_order` (`WORLD` persisted plus non-persisted blocks) and `bind_order` (blocks with a `binding_source`, ascending `String(block_id)`, § 6). The plan is immutable after the freeze and printable (`describe()`), like the hook schedule.
146	
147	Registering more than `MAX_BLOCKS` blocks fails boot with `BLOCK_LIMIT` (**new code**) at the first excess registration (TR-cmd-035). The cost of the sort at `MAX_BLOCKS` is a one-time O(n²) over at most that many entries.
148	
149	**2.3 The tie-break is load-bearing.** Probe P2 shows several valid orders of the same MVP graph under different tie-breaks. Any block that reads a non-predecessor's derived state would work under one and fail under another. That is the point of making the order a total function of registration data and of testing against other linear extensions (§ 8): the rule "a block depends only on what it declares" is enforced by the permutation test, not by trust.
150	
151	**2.4 The MVP order** (computed 2026-10-29 by a throwaway script applying § 2.2 to the architecture's registration order, Layout, Graph, Body, Controller, Emitter, Suit, Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror, Sanity; the kernel prints the authoritative order at the freeze and this table is illustrative):
152	
153	| Pos | Block | `restore_after` (from the owner GDD or ADR) | Source |
154	|---|---|---|---|
155	| 0 | `kernel.clock` | (kernel-internal, installed at R2, not in the DAG) | ADR-0003 § 10 |
156	| 1 | `layout.state` | `[]` (the root) | ADR-0013 § 1 |
157	| 2 | `graph.state` | `[layout.state]` | ADR-0011 § 1 |
158	| 3 | `body.state` | `[layout.state]` | BDY-5 |
159	| 4 | `suit.state` | `[]` | SE-34 |
160	| 5 | `controller.state` | `[body.state, suit.state]` | ADR-0019 § 2.1 |
161	| 6 | `emitter.state` | `[layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]` | EM-1 |
162	| 7 | `interaction.state` | `[layout.state, controller.state, graph.state, body.state, emitter.state]` | IA-36 |
163	| 8 | `assembly.state` | `[layout.state, graph.state, interaction.state, body.state]` | MSA-4 |
164	| 9 | `web.state` | `[layout.state, graph.state, body.state]` | WM-2 |
165	| 10 | `attention.state` | `[graph.state, emitter.state]` | AT registration |
166	| 11 | `horror.state` | `[layout.state, graph.state, emitter.state, attention.state]` | HE-3 |
167	| 12 | `sanity.state` | `[]` | SN-1 |
168	| 13 | `sanity.ledger` | `[sanity.state, graph.state, layout.state, horror.state]` | SN-1 |
169	| 14 | `sanity.perception` | non-persisted; **assumed** `[sanity.state, sanity.ledger]` (the GDD gives none; Open Question 1) | SN-1 |
170	
171	That is 13 persisted blocks plus the clock (the 14 of SL-19) and one derived block. The DAG is acyclic: Layout is the only root of the layout chain, Suit and Sanity have no outgoing edge to the Controller or each other, and the Controller's edges go only to Body and Suit (verified by reading the owner GDDs; neither Body nor Suit declares an edge back, ADR-0019's cross-ADR assumption).
172	
173	### 3. The block contract at restore: two phases, three read tiers
174	
175	**3.1 Two phases per block, restated once (ADR-0006 § 2.2 is the rule; this ADR adds the pass-level consequences).** `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` decodes and validates into scratch (phase 1, cold path, allocation allowed, **no write to the live block**), then, on success only, copies the contents into the existing block object and rebuilds the block's *static* derived members (phase 2). A failure is `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*, detail)` with the live block untouched. The scratch object must contain no reference cycle (probe P3: a cycle leaks and `OBJECT_COUNT` shows it).
176	
177	**3.2 What `restore` may read.** Its own `data`, and **Tier S** reads of blocks in its transitive `restore_after` closure (§ 3.4). It writes only its own block. It never calls another owner's mutator, never reads `kernel.clock` `T` for a decision (the clock is installed at R2 and is read-only), and never reads a non-predecessor.
178	
179	**3.3 Defaults go through `restore`.** `default_state(ctx)` of a persisted block ends with `ctx.put(payload)` where `payload` has the shape and `schema_version` of a snapshot; the kernel applies it by calling **that block's own `restore`** with `stored_version = schema_version`. One copy path means the default is validated on every new game and every absent-block restore, a `default_state` that its own `restore` rejects fails the first test that builds a world, and the block's "registered-but-unrestored" hash (ADR-0011 § 4.6, ADR-0013 `counters` at 1) is what restore produces. If a persisted block's `default_state` returns without `put`, the pass faults with `DEFAULT_STATE_NO_PAYLOAD` (**new code**). For a non-persisted block `default_state` only resets derived members and `put` is not expected.
180	
181	**3.4 Read tiers across blocks.** Every read-view method of every block is documented as one of two tiers (a doc tag read by the lint of § 8 and printed by the Debug Overlay):
182	
183	- **Tier S (persisted-answerable).** Answerable from the block's persisted columns and the static derived members its `restore` rebuilt. Valid as soon as that block's `restore` returned. Layout's class 1 (`room_at`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `socket_plan`, `section_offset`, `body_of`, static rects; ADR-0013 § 10, TR-section-008), the Graph's `opening_into`, `seam_openings_into`, `section_counts_into`, `RoomSource` and `step_no`, Body's `seat_bindings()`, and any `ids below next_*` check are Tier S.
184	- **Tier D (derived).** Needs the block's own `post_restore`. Layout's class 2 (door-leaf rects, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `door_passage_into`), the Graph's served and band caches, the Emitter's static layer. Before the owner's `post_restore` ran, a Tier D read returns the template default (or neutral value) and raises the owner's `stale_*` diagnostic (Layout's `stale_leaf` is the first instance).
185	
186	The rule that makes order matter and keeps it checkable: **in `post_restore(X)` the callable may read Tier S of any block and Tier D only of blocks that precede X in the DAG's closure.** `restore` is stricter: Tier S of closure predecessors only. No hook, command or presentation read happens between the stages, so a stale read can occur only inside the pass.
187	
188	### 4. The `post_restore` contract
189	
190	**4.1 Order.** `post_restore` runs in `post_order`, which is `order` filtered; it is the same DAG as `restore`. Reasons: architecture § Data Flow 7 already states it; Emitter Open Question 26 and ADR-0019 (Controller after Suit) need it; the cost is zero because the DAG exists; and "informational only" (Layout) means no rule depends on it, which is compatible. After this ADR Layout's `version`/`leaf_version` self-heal (LY-12 d) stays as belt and braces and is no longer what makes the Emitter's cold build correct for open doors.
191	
192	**4.2 Write policy (closed).**
193	
194	| Class | May `post_restore(X)` do it? | Rule |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| Rebuild X's **derived** members (caches, lookups, version counters, seeds of last-emitted values) | Yes | Writes no persisted column and draws no RNG. |
197	| Write X's **persisted** columns | **No**, except block X is on `REBASE_BLOCKS` (§ 9) | A normalisation belongs in `snapshot()`; see § 9. |
198	| Write any **other** block | **No** | `open_for` of another block in the `RESTORE` scope is `REFUSED` and a counted `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` violation (ADR-0003 § 4). |
199	| Submit a command | **No** (impossible) | `SnapshotContext` has no `submit_system`. |
200	| Clamp, prune, repair or default a persisted value | **No** | A bad value is a fault; a well-formed but semantically dead reference restores as it is (TR-sanity-019). |
201	| Raise a fault | Yes | Only for a check of § 5; first failure wins. |
202	
203	**4.3 Reconciliation is an ordinary hook rule, not a restore step.** Anything a block would like to "fix up after a load" (the Graph's stock reconcile, Interaction's subject window, Attention's beacon, Sanity's dead-subject prune) is performed by the owner's **next hook run under a normal `HOOK` scope**, and it must be **the same rule that runs every tick**, a no-op when state is consistent, with no `just_restored` flag. Reason: kernel G4 demands the same `state_hash` at every tick from a restored run and an uninterrupted run; a reconcile that exists only on the first post-restore run would diverge from the uninterrupted run whenever it does anything, and a reconcile that does nothing in the uninterrupted run is exactly an idempotent steady-state rule. KRN-RST-11 checks each owner's reconcile this way (600 ticks, hash per tick).
204	
205	**4.4 Consequences for the cited rows.**
206	- **Layout/Graph stock reconcile (TR-itemdb-033).** The Graph keeps ADR-0011 § 7.3: a store above a lowered live `stock_cap` restores byte-identically (it is below the physical ceiling `max_stock_*`), and the clamp, the `discarded_*` credit, the `stock_clamped` count and the diagnostic naming node, old stock and cap run at the head of phase 0 of the first Graph step. `post_restore` does not clamp (§ 4.2), so the K-4 verdict is `MATCH` and no REBASED cause is owed to ADR-0006.
207	- **Catalogue tuning drift (TR-itemdb-032).** A `restore` or `post_restore` check is either **structural** (shape, range, id order, reference resolution, a physical ceiling) or it is not a restore check. A value that is a catalogue tunable (mass, `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G`, `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX`, `PATCH_CAP_BP`, `stock_cap`, a def's rated output) is never asserted, clamped, deleted or migrated at restore. A `def_id` that no longer resolves is a structural failure (`RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`), and an alias renamed by ADR-0007's path resolves.
208	- **Interaction (TR-interact-016, -017, TR-boarding-005).** § 5 row V-IA and § 9: Interaction's `post_restore` may not write the Emitter or the Controller; `loose[].inst` decode is a verifier; channel and door-attempt dropping is an interim normalisation.
209	- **Body (TR-shipbody-010).** `pos_prev := pos_curr` is a derived-member rebuild; `sub` is preserved (persisted, untouched); the trapped-actor probe counts and never faults; Body never rebuilds the kernel seat binding.
210	- **Attention (TR-attention-025).** `post_restore` rebuilds caches only; the beacon is reconciled by the first `attention.step` by comparing persisted `beacon_commanded` with Emitter state (§ 4.3); no cue fires on load because cues fire on transitions and the kernel's `ALL` batch carries no transition.
211	- **Sanity (TR-sanity-019).** `post_restore` must not prune; a well-formed dead `subject_ref` restores, is projected as it is and is invalidated by the next hook run.
212	
213	### 5. Cross-block verification: where the checks live and the order they run in
214	
215	**5.1 Decision.** Verifiers are **distributed, never kernel-held**. Each is a pure, read-only function in the owning block's `restore` or `verify` file, called from that block's `post_restore` (or `restore` where the check needs only Tier S of a predecessor), at the block's position in the DAG. The kernel only runs the callables in order and turns the first fault into `FAULTED`. This keeps H1 (no domain rule in the kernel), keeps the TR rows' wording ("in `post_restore`"), and needs no new registrar surface. The central artefact is **this ADR's numbered list**, which fixes what is checked and in which block's slot; the owner ADRs fix the check bodies.
216	
217	**5.2 Verifier shape.** A verifier is `static func verify_restore(views: <Owner>VerifierViews, out: VerifyOut) -> int` returning `0` or a packed fault code of the owner's domain, with the invariant id and two ints written to the caller-owned `out` (no allocation; a Class A shape in the sense of ADR-0003 § 5). `<Owner>VerifierViews` is a plain `RefCounted` holding the read-view facades the check needs (SIM views only, never a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block), built by the composition root at `setup`. The block's `post_restore` does `var rc := X.verify_restore(views, out); if rc != 0: ctx.fault(rc, out.detail()); return ctx.complete()`. The same function is reused unchanged by runtime assertions (Assembly's release subset, § 5.4). Fault names follow `<DOMAIN>_RESTORE_<REASON>` for a `restore` check and `<DOMAIN>_VERIFY_<INV>` for a cross-block `post_restore` check, both in the owner's static domain (ADR-0003 § 6).
218	
219	**5.3 The numbered list, in DAG order.** (Details of each check live in the cited owner document; "T" marks a check that reads Tier S only, so it is order-independent.)

225	| V3 | `graph.state` restore | The twelve ordered steps of ADR-0011 § 7.2 | own data, catalog | `GRAPH_RESTORE_*` (3) | ADR-0011 |
226	| V4 | `graph.state` post_restore | Compartment `room_ref` resolves through `RoomSource` (`RESTORE_UNKNOWN_ROOM`); `n_o2 + n_inert` within `P_MAX x V x GAS_SCALE`; LS-24 structural invariants | Layout T and own | `GRAPH_RESTORE_*` (3) | ADR-0011 § 7.4 |
227	| V5 | `body.state` restore | Types, counts, row fields, order, canonicity, then every `body_id` live in Layout (`BDY_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BODY`) | Layout T | `BDY_RESTORE_*` (5) | BDY-31, ADR-0015 |

229	| V7 | `suit.state` post_restore | Held and carried instances decode with `from_array(a, graph_step_no)` (`graph_step_no` = the restored Graph's absolute 10 Hz `step_no`, Tier S); wrong length or element type `SUIT_RESTORE_INSTANCE_FORM`; `validate_instance` failure; `controller.state.carry_ref == suit.state.carried_id` or both NONE (`SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`); seat row has a Body seat (`_SEAT_UNBOUND`) | Graph T, Controller T, Body T, Item DB | `SUIT_RESTORE_*` (9) | SE-13, TR-suit-012, TR-boarding-005, ADR-0027 |
230	| V8 | `controller.state` post_restore | Derived recompute only (`chest_sim`, `hand_sim`, `cap_seen`); no verifier | Body T, Suit D (Suit precedes) | none | ADR-0019 § 2.7 |

246	### 6. The binding rebuild (half (b))
247	
248	**6.1 Registration.** A block that owns an entity a PlayerId acts as registers `BlockDescriptor.binding_source` at `BOOTING` (ADR-0003 § 2; the binding source is this field only). At the MVP: `body.state` (`seat_bindings() -> [(seat, actor_id)]`, ascending seat, `SEAT` rows only, derived per call; TR-shipbody-030) and `emitter.state` (`beam_bindings() -> [(player_id, beam_id)]`, ascending `player_id`, pure read; TR-emitter-009). `controller.state` is not a source: it stores the PlayerId and resolves the actor through Body (ADR-0019 § 2.1).
249	
250	**6.2 Payload form.** `binding_source(ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken` delivers through `ctx.put(pairs)` one **flat `PackedInt64Array`** `[player_id_0, entity_id_0, player_id_1, entity_id_1, ...]`, strictly ascending by `(player_id, entity_id)`, so no per-pair `Array` is allocated. The callable is a pure read: it receives no `WriteScope` and runs after every `post_restore`, so it reads rebuilt state.
251	
252	**6.3 The rebuild.** At R6/N6, after the verdict and as the last step of every pass, the kernel iterates `bind_order` (ascending **`String(block_id)`** of the source, the comparison of probe P1; a `StringName` comparison or `sort()` is forbidden, lint RST-01) and for each source: calls it, validates the array (even length; `player_id >= 1`; strictly ascending), and binds each pair as `player_id -> (source block, entity_id)` into the `PlayerBindings` object (ADR-0002 § 4). A key `(source block, entity_id)` delivered for two different PlayerIds, or the same `(player_id, source, entity_id)` delivered twice, or a malformed array, or a source that called `ctx.fault` or returned without the token, is `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT` (domain 0 code 3) with detail `{reason, source, player_id, entity_id}` where `reason` is one of `CONFLICT_OWNER`, `DUPLICATE_TRIPLE`, `SHAPE`, `ORDER`, `PLAYER_RANGE`, `SOURCE_FAULT`. Equal entity numbers from two sources (Body actor 1, Emitter beam 1) are two keys and never conflict; comparisons are within one source. The rebuild is not a control-plane request and no command can interleave (the pass is one boundary service).
253	
254	**6.4 Consequences.** Half (b) is never saved, never read from the payload and never written by a block (TR-saveload-037); the first `RUNNING` tick passes the authority check for PlayerId 1 against `(body.state, avatar actor)` and `(emitter.state, beam)` (KRN-RST-06 submits an `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` command on tick 1 of a restored run); Body's `post_restore` does not rebuild it (TR-shipbody-010); a fault leaves half (b) empty (§ 1.3). Half (a) (`peer_id -> PlayerId`) is never touched by a pass.

256	### 7. Pass timing and diagnostics
257	
258	Per block and stage the kernel records `t_restore(b)` and `t_post(b)` through the injected `Clock` port (`now_us()`, ADR-0006 § Constraints, SIM-02 applies: logged, never branched on), plus `t_verdict` and `t_rebind`, into the `LoadTiming` diagnostics record. The sum is the `loading_ms` of the kernel GDD's load-budget formula; the per-owner figures (Graph `restore` plus `post_restore` at most 2 ms; the MVP world at most 3 ms with a 10 ms ceiling, TR-lsg-036) are checked by KRN-RST-14 against the registry names `LOADING_TARGET_MS` and the Graph's, reported and never a cut-off. A pass above its owner's figure is a diagnostic, like `STEP_BUDGET_MS`.

260	### 8. Tests that make the rules falsifiable
261	
262	- **Order-permutation (G4) test, KRN-RST-05.** For a fixed seeded world, snapshot at tick `T`, then restore into fresh kernels whose `RestorePlan` is replaced by each of at least four **other valid linear extensions** of the same DAG (smallest id first, largest id first, reverse registration, and a seeded shuffle of ready lists), run 120 ticks each, and compare the per-tick `state_hash` trace and a battery of read-view answers (`lit`, `top_emitter`, `room_at`, `served_pm`, door-leaf rects, seat bindings) with the uninterrupted run. A block that read a non-predecessor's unbuilt derived state, or depended on the wiring order, fails here.
263	- **Reconciliation symmetry, KRN-RST-11** (§ 4.3), per owner that defers a reconcile.
264	- **Fault ladder, KRN-RST-04.** For every stage and every block of the MVP fixture a stub injects `ctx.fault`; the test asserts the recorded `LoadFailure`, that no later callable ran, that no tick, `ALL` batch or `load_seq` increment happened, that `FAULTED` rejects commands and snapshots, and that a following good `request_restore` matches a fresh kernel.
265	- **Lint pack RST** (proposed to ADR-0010 § 6 as a new pack): **RST-01** (error, `src/kernel`, `src/save`, `src/shared`): `<`, `>` or `.sort()` applied to a `StringName` operand or an `Array[StringName]`, outside the one helper `BlockIdOrder.less(a: StringName, b: StringName)` which compares `String(a) < String(b)`. **RST-02** (error, `src/sim`): a file named `*_restore.gd` or `*_verify.gd` references no other block's mutator class (the class map of ADR-0010 § 2.1 lists them); the run-time fence is the `RESTORE` scope. **RST-03** (error, whole `src/`): `init_world(` is called only from `src/kernel/` (the pass driver); owners define it and never call it. A fourth rule is a test, not a lint: **RST-04** every registered persisted block has a `FixtureFactory` entry (§ 9).

267	### 9. Idempotence, fixtures and `REBASE_BLOCKS`
268	
269	**9.1 Rule.** Every persisted block is restore-idempotent: `snapshot -> encode -> decode -> restore -> snapshot` yields equal canonical bytes (ADR-0006 § 2.2). The way to get there is **normalise in `snapshot()`, not in `post_restore`**: a transient field the block would clear on restore (an in-progress channel, a door attempt, a pending completion, a controller ramp) is written in its cleared form by `snapshot()` while the live block keeps its value, so the restore reproduces the saved bytes exactly and `post_restore` has nothing to write. Assembly (`pending` written NONE, TR-assembly-012) and the Controller (PC-17) already do this.
270	
271	**9.2 `FixtureFactory` and the generic harness (TR-saveload-034).** Each persisted block registers, in the test tree only, a `FixtureFactory` with `empty() -> Dictionary` (equal to its `default_state` payload), `typical(seed) -> Dictionary` and `extreme(seed) -> Dictionary` (caps reached, tombstones present, counters near limits). `tests/unit/restore/idempotence_test.gd` **enumerates the registry** (never a hand list), and for every persisted block and fixture asserts the round trip, that `default_state` equals `empty()`, and that the block restores from its own `default_state` payload. A persisted block without a factory fails RST-04.
272	
273	**9.3 `REBASE_BLOCKS` is a checked list, not a convention.** The build constant `REBASE_BLOCKS` (Save/Load, SL-12) is a committed array in `src/save/` with one data row per member in `tests/fixtures/rebase_blocks.json`: `{block_id, owner_adr, reason, exit}`. CI fails if (a) a block is idempotent under § 9.2 but listed (a stale entry) or non-idempotent but not listed; (b) a build tagged for an outside release has a non-empty list. The gate flips with the same project-level `SHIPPED` decision as ADR-0007's id ledgers and ADR-0006 § 2.6. **Interim members at the MVP: `interaction.state`**, whose `post_restore` drops in-progress channels, door attempts and `last_result` and resolves a RESERVED FULL-job part (IA-36; OQ-39). Its exit is ADR-0020's: move those clears into `snapshot()` (the saved payload carries the dropped form and the resolved part), after which `post_restore` only rebuilds `W`. An older, un-normalised payload is still handled by a tolerant restore, as a migration. No other MVP block needs the list: `layout.state`'s geometry-hash rewrite (ADR-0013 § 10 drift policy) occurs only on a content change and is accepted as a REBASED case, not a standing member.
274	
275	### 10. Resource lifetime across passes (TR-light-037, this ADR's half)
276	
277	A pass must leave the object, node and orphan-node counts where the previous pass left them: scratch objects are acyclic and dropped at the end of the owner's `restore`; contexts, scopes, tokens and read-view facades are the kernel's and the owners' long-lived objects, re-armed rather than rebuilt (ADR-0003 § 3, § 7); `restore` copies into the existing block, so no facade or pool handle goes stale. KRN-RST-10 alternates `request_restore` and `request_new_game` 100 times on the headless kernel and asserts that `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT`, `OBJECT_NODE_COUNT` and `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` after cycle *n* equal those after cycle 1 (probe P4: all three monitors are readable headless; probe P3: a retained cycle is detected). ADR-0028 extends the same loop with the build, body-swap and render-texture legs and the light and occluder pools; this ADR guarantees only that the pass itself leaks nothing.

341	### Implementation Guidelines
342	- **Must** drive restore, `post_restore`, `default_state` and `init_world` from the one compiled `RestorePlan`; **must never** iterate a `Dictionary` or the registry's insertion order to order them.
343	- **Must** compare and sort block ids as `String` through `BlockIdOrder.less`; **must never** apply `<`, `>` or `.sort()` to `StringName` values (probe P1).
344	- **Must** run the pre-check over the whole payload before any owner callable or kernel write; **must never** call a `restore()` on the strength of a partially checked payload.
345	- **Must** stop the pass at the first fault and enter `FAULTED`; **must never** continue to later blocks, deliver an `ALL` batch, increment `load_seq`, or accept a snapshot after a faulted pass.
346	- **Must** apply a `default_state` payload through the block's own `restore`; **must never** let `default_state` write the live block directly.
347	- **Must** make `post_restore` rebuild derived members only (§ 4.2); **must never** clamp, prune, repair, default or write a persisted value or another block from it, except a `REBASE_BLOCKS` member's documented normalisation.
348	- **Must** express every after-load fix-up as the owner's ordinary hook rule that is a no-op on consistent state (§ 4.3); **must never** key behaviour on "first run after restore".
349	- **Must** read only Tier S of non-predecessors and only closure predecessors in `restore`; **must** tag every read-view method S or D in its doc comment.
350	- **Must** put verifier code in `*_verify.gd` as a pure `static` function returning 0 or a packed code and reuse it for runtime assertions; **must never** put a cross-block rule in the kernel.
351	- **Must** deliver binding pairs as a strictly ascending flat `PackedInt64Array` from a pure read; **must never** write the binding table, rebuild it from a block, or save it.
352	- **Must** keep restore scratch objects free of reference cycles and drop them before `restore` returns.
353	- **Must** register a `FixtureFactory` for every persisted block and keep `REBASE_BLOCKS` equal to the measured non-idempotent set.
354	- **Must never** call `init_world` outside the pass driver, or in a restore pass.

406	## Consequences
407	
408	### Positive
409	- One sequence for restore and one for new game, each with a named failure state; the "faulted `LOADING` never plays" guarantee is stated and tested.
410	- `post_restore` order is declared data; the Emitter's cold build no longer depends on a self-heal, and any hidden dependency is caught by the permutation test.
411	- The post_restore write policy is one table every owner can check; deferred fix-ups become ordinary hook rules, so G4 holds by construction.
412	- Verifiers are listed once, owned by their blocks, reused at runtime, and the first failure is deterministic (fuzzable).
413	- The `REBASE_BLOCKS` exit is a CI gate with a named owner, not a convention.
414	- A real engine trap (StringName ordering) is found, fenced by a lint and a helper, and tested.
415	
416	### Negative
417	- Five foundation changes (three kernel codes, two pass codes, an outcome record) and one new lint pack are asked of ADR-0003, ADR-0002 and ADR-0010.
418	- Interaction must change its design from "re-register at `post_restore`" to "detect at `post_restore`, repair in the hook", and move its normalisation into `snapshot()` before the first outside build.
419	- The pass stops at the first fault, so a corrupt save reports one problem at a time.
420	- A failed load cannot return the player to the pre-load world; the fallback is another generation.
421	- The permutation test multiplies the cost of every restore-affecting change in CI.
422	
423	## Risks
424	- **R1: a block quietly depends on registration order.** Mitigation: KRN-RST-05 across at least four linear extensions on the MVP fixture, run on every push; a failing hash trace names the first diverging tick and block.
425	- **R2: Tier S/Tier D tags drift from the code.** Mitigation: the tags are doc comments read by a lint of the same pack and printed by the Debug Overlay; the permutation test is the semantic check. Residual risk is accepted until the lint pack is built.
426	- **R3: a deferred reconcile is not a no-op in the uninterrupted run.** Mitigation: KRN-RST-11 compares 600 ticks per owner; an owner that cannot make its fix-up idempotent files an ADR amendment before its story closes.
427	- **R4: the `kernel.clock` payload entry's shape (`tick_rate`) is not yet fixed by ADR-0006.** Mitigation: Open Question 2 and a foundation ask; until settled the `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` pre-check cannot run on a payload without it.
428	- **R5: GDScript cost of a full pass is unmeasured** (Verification 2). Mitigation: it is a logged diagnostic, not a gate; S1 and SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE decide whether any rung is needed.
429	- **R6: `sanity.perception` has no declared `restore_after`.** Mitigation: assumed edges in § 2.4; if ADR-0025 declares none it can run before the blocks it rebuilds from. Open Question 1.
430	- **R7: a future PROFILE block's cold-open ordering is untested** at zero MVP blocks. Mitigation: the plan already visits `PROFILE` blocks in the cold-open pass; a story builds the test with the first PROFILE block.
431	- **R8: the proposed verifier V11 (one-holder) is outside Interaction's closed reason list.** Mitigation: it is marked proposed; accept or drop it with ADR-0020 (Open Question 3).

470	## Performance Implications
471	- **CPU**: One-time DAG compile at the freeze, O(n²) over at most `MAX_BLOCKS` blocks. A pass is the sum of the owners' `restore` and `post_restore` plus a handful of kernel steps (about two `Callable.call` per block, three stages); owner figures are the Graph's `restore` plus `post_restore` at most 2 ms and the MVP world at most 3 ms with a 10 ms ceiling (TR-lsg-036), all UNVERIFIED on a release export (S1, SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE). The pass is one boundary service and may exceed a frame; the Pipeline holds the black quad (`LOADING_TARGET_MS`, `t_hold_pad`). The binding rebuild is O(sources x players) with players at most 4. Assembly's release verifier subset is its own allocation (`verifier_release`).
472	- **Memory**: `RestorePlan` is five `PackedInt32Array`s of at most `MAX_BLOCKS`; scratch objects are transient and acyclic; no new retained structure.
473	- **Load Time**: Inside `loading_ms` of the kernel GDD; pre-check and file decode are Save/Load's and off the main thread when hot.
474	- **Network**: None. The order is a pure function of registration data, so a co-op guest running the same build restores identically (VS-B).

I'm also looking at how packed arrays behave when passed by value versus exposed as public members on RestorePlan—since consumers get copy-on-write copies, claims about immutability aren't actually enforceable since callers could still mutate their own copy's elements directly.

Separately, I'm checking whether Callables create reference cycles—they store an ObjectID rather than a strong reference, so holding a Callable to self shouldn't leak, though lambdas capturing self directly do create a real strong reference and could.

I'm also verifying whether sorting typed arrays like Array[StringName] violates the RST-01 lint rule, and whether String/StringName comparison operators use code-point ordering that's locale-independent.

This confirms it: `AlphCompare` exists specifically because `operator<` does raw pointer comparison, which depends on allocator/ASLR behavior and could vary between process runs even with identical scripts — making it genuinely unsafe to rely on for deterministic ordering.

I also want to confirm that `PackedStringArray.sort()` behaves alphabetically as expected, and that Dictionary iteration order is insertion-based in Godot 4, which the ADR correctly sidesteps. Checking other parts of the design too — the `LoadStage` enum usage, the `LoadFailure` class structure, and whether the `restore()` callable override with typed return `CompletionToken` is consistent with Godot 4.7's typed-return override rules.

One subtle engine concern I'm tracking: when a script error occurs mid-call inside a `Callable.call`, the function typically returns null rather than throwing, so the token-check logic needs to handle that gracefully. I also need to verify that the `restore` phase doesn't mutate or retain the `data` Dictionary it receives, since Dictionaries are passed by reference and the decoded payload could end up aliased into live state unintentionally.

Thinking about aliasing risk further — if restore copies nested Arrays or Dictionaries without a deep copy, the live block and the payload could end up sharing references, which is dangerous if the payload gets reused by Save/Load for a retry. I'm flagging that restore should use `duplicate(true)` on nested reference types, while packed arrays are safe since they're copy-on-write value types; this feels like a medium-severity, non-blocking finding worth noting.

I run through a series of smaller timing and type checks — epoch bounds, tick rate ints, clock injection, atomicity of the LOADING phase, O(n²) claims, Kahn's algorithm using smallest ready index — and each one checks out as fine or plausible, including the claim about StringName ordering potentially mattering.

adr-0005-determinism-keyed-rng-canonical-encoding-and-hashing.md:287:The reason for the change: the bytewise order of the *encoded* integer key puts `3, 10` before `-5` and orders strings by length first, because the encoded key begins with a little-endian length. That order is deterministic but meaningless, and the diff the G4 test prints ("the first differing `block_id` and key") reads naturally only in value order. Value order is also what `Array.sort()` gives with no custom comparator, so the encoder needs no byte-comparison helper (GDScript cannot order two `PackedByteArray`s). Both orders are equally injective, so the change costs nothing in collision safety, and no hash exists yet. `gdd_sync` item for the kernel GDD D.12 and KRN-HASH-01.
adr-0005-determinism-keyed-rng-canonical-encoding-and-hashing.md:315:- **(b) Unpacking idiom.** `match typeof(value)`, then a typed assignment (`var d: Dictionary = value`, `var i: int = value`), **never `as`**: `UNSAFE_CAST` at error rejects `value as Dictionary` on a `Variant`, while the typed assignment loads cleanly (P20). Dictionary keys go into typed arrays: `var ks: Array[int] = []; ks.assign(d.keys())` for an all-int dictionary, and `var ss: Array[String] = []; ss.assign(d.keys())` for the string family (a `StringName` key becomes its `String`, P20), then `ks.sort()` or `ss.sort()`. The dictionary is classified first (`typeof` over its keys), so `assign` never sees a mix; the bare `Array` that `Dictionary.keys()` returns is consumed only by `assign`, so no `Array` token appears in source. The public helpers are `CanonicalEncoder.sorted_int_keys(d)` and `CanonicalEncoder.sorted_string_keys(d)`.

adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md:217:**Stage 0 holds three registrants, and their order is declared, not incidental.** The layout projector, `body.projector` and Lighting's occluder builder all register at `PROJECT`. Within a stage the order is therefore **registration order, fixed by the composition root**, and a descriptor that needs a same-stage predecessor names it in `after`; `freeze()` fails boot if a named predecessor is not registered earlier in the same stage. This aligns with ADR-0003, though I'm noting a potential tension: the SnapshotContext holds a reference to the payload dictionary during restore, and once re-armed that reference needs to be cleared afterward to avoid stale retention.

I'm also checking minor details—whether the restore flow shares the same context object as default_state, confirming fault classes stay uninstantiated, verifying typed array declarations are fine, and double-checking error codes like RESTORE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED against ADR-0006. The Kahn algorithm's smallest-ready-index approach being O(n²) is acceptable here.

Now I'm looking at how String versus StringName keys behave in payload dictionaries—Godot 4 merges them when text matches, so lookups like checking for "layout.state" should work fine, though the precheck still needs explicit StringName conversion when comparing against the registry. More interesting is the ordering question: since Dictionary.keys() preserves insertion order and that order comes from decoding the payload, if two unknown keys exist, which one gets named in the first failure depends on decode order rather than registry order—this seems to conflict with the claim that the precheck is a pure function of the payload, since true determinism would want it to iterate registry order instead of payload insertion order.

I'm also flagging that the reset test checking object counts across 100 cycles wouldn't catch leaks from self-referential Arrays or Dictionaries, or lambdas capturing self, since those don't show up in ObjectDB counts the same way—worth recommending a static memory usage check and a lint rule against self-referential containers as a non-blocking improvement.

On P4, RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED reads as 0 under the headless dummy renderer, so any texture-memory assertion there is vacuous rather than confirming availability; that needs a windowed run instead, consistent with the existing ADR note. I also notice get_monitor returns floats being compared with integer assertions in places, which is a minor type mismatch worth fixing with explicit int() casts. Checking whether the typed-return override rule from ADR-0016 has exceptions in the fixture and verification classes—so far nothing overrides it, though I want to confirm Callable-based shapes don't trigger the rule unexpectedly.

Now looking at whether RestorePlan's array element writes bypass setters—since rebuilt arrays get assigned wholesale, that seems fine, and the explicit touch_serial increment in open_for covers the hash-cache reset concern even though it's not going through a setter. I'm also flagging that compile() takes a bare untyped Array parameter, which may conflict with the typed-array rule—need to check whether that ban applies specifically to src/shared or extends to src/kernel where RestorePlan lives.

I'm noting that ADR-0017's claim about registrants re-registering idempotently during their own post_restore conflicts with ADR-0016 §4.2 and V10, which is a cross-ADR inconsistency worth flagging. I also see a smaller discrepancy where ADR-0015's post_restore derives `world_prev`, but ADR-0016 §4.4 only mentions `pos_prev`, plus ADR-0015 V6 shows Body's post_restore re-checking Layout live.

I'm checking the §2.4 table entries for Body and Graph against ADR-0015 for consistency, and tracing the DAG ordering rule where all restores must complete before any post_restore runs, confirming Tier S reads of Graph and Layout are valid at that point. I'm also confirming the pass executes synchronously within a single boundary service with no async calls, and that the idempotence harness (snapshot → encode → decode → restore → snapshot equal canonical bytes) holds up, so now I'm ready to write up these findings concisely.

Moving to the enumeration of issues: E1 flags a duplicate class_name within one listed file in Key Interfaces, which I'm marking non-blocking but low severity despite the literal copy breaking. E2 flags bare `Array`/`Dictionary` types in RestorePlan.compile and LoadFailure/restore signatures that violate ADR-0010's typing rule, requiring them to be typed as `Array[BlockDescriptor]` and similar, and noting this creates a caller-compatibility issue plus a cross-ADR dependency on an allow-list entry. E3 covers my own verification of the P1 characterization — the mechanism depends on pointer/intern order, and reversing creation order produced alphabetical output, meaning "stable across two runs" doesn't actually imply determinism.

I'm noting this should cite ADR-0005 P12 for stronger grounding, and that StringName comparisons are accepted by the analyzer while mixed StringName/String comparisons correctly fail to parse, so RST-01 needs to be type-aware — this is non-blocking and low severity, though it duplicates ADR-0005's AST rule under ADR-0010's ownership.

E4 addresses a blind spot in KRN-RST-10: OBJECT_COUNT only tracks Objects, so Array/Dictionary self-reference cycles and self-capturing lambdas in RefCounted leak invisibly, as I verified with probes showing zero OBJECT_COUNT delta despite real memory growth. I'm proposing adding a debug-only MEMORY_STATIC check, banning self-referencing containers and self-capturing stored lambdas, and noting monitors return floats that need int() comparison — medium severity, non-blocking.

E5 starts describing a vacuous P4 result where RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED reads zero under the headless dummy renderer, meaning a readable metric doesn't guarantee a meaningful measurement.

I'm now extending this point: legs involving textures need the windowed lane from ADR-0010, and OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT's debug-only status is uncertain enough that it should be flagged UNVERIFIED in release builds — low severity, non-blocking.

E6 examines R1(a)'s pre-check, which iterates payload Dictionary keys in insertion/decoder order, and the claim that failure detection is deterministic and a pure function of payload needs refinement: registry order should govern cases (c) and (d), while sorted String keys should govern the unknown case (a), and I'm also flagging that Dictionary treats String and StringName keys as equal per ADR-0005 — medium, non-blocking.

E7 looks at restore aliasing: since Dictionary and nested Array/Dictionary are references while packed arrays are COW values, Phase 2's "copy contents into existing block" step must deep-copy nested containers or build typed columns explicitly, otherwise the live block ends up aliasing the staged payload still held by Save/Load/ctx — and the kernel also needs to clear ctx's put slot after applying the default payload.

Continuing E7, I'm also noting that the same SnapshotContext gets passed to both default_state and restore, so the put slot must be moved out before restore re-arms it — another medium, non-blocking issue, and JSON number handling isn't relevant here.

E8 flags that KRN-RST-05's "seeded shuffle of ready lists" can't rely on Array.shuffle() or randi since those use the banned global RNG under DET-01 — it needs its own DetRng/Fisher-Yates stream instead, low severity.

E9 raises a concern about RestorePlan's "immutable" PackedInt32Array exposed as a public var — since GDScript has no readonly and index writes go through even though local reads are COW copies, I should swap this for a private backing array with accessor functions like order_at(i) and size(), or a setup-based setter. But then I hit something more interesting: ADR-0014's probe claims that a local alias of a RefCounted member PackedInt64Array actually writes through to the member, which contradicts my earlier assumption that packed arrays are COW values — in fact Godot 4 documents packed arrays as being passed by reference, not copy-on-write, meaning my earlier statement was wrong. This has real implications: ctx.put(PackedInt64Array) could hand the kernel a live reference to the owner's array, RestorePlan.order reads could be externally mutable, and restore's packed payload columns could end up aliasing the original payload unless explicitly duplicated — I need to probe this directly to confirm the exact reference semantics before relying on any of it.

input.verdict: CONCERNS (engine): no blocking engine error. No API is deprecated, post-cutoff or mis-signed. The probed claims P1 and P3 reproduce on 4.7.2. Seven non-blocking amendments are needed before Acceptance. Three matter most: packed-array reference semantics at restore (E3), the blind spot in the KRN-RST-10 leak guard (E4), and one non-compiling Key Interfaces listing (E1).

findings.text: Key Interfaces puts `class_name LoadStage` and `class_name LoadFailure` under a single `# src/kernel/load_stage.gd` header. A GDScript file allows one `class_name`, so copying the block verbatim will not parse. The other listings (RestorePlan, BlockIdOrder, VerifyOut, FixtureFactory) each have a header and are fine. The `LoadStage` int constants are legal GDScript.
findings.amendment: Add a `# src/kernel/load_failure.gd` header above `class_name LoadFailure`. State that each listed class is its own file, as ADR-0003 does for fault classes.

findings.text: The Key Interfaces use bare `Array` and `Dictionary`: `RestorePlan.compile(blocks: Array, max_blocks: int, out_errors: Array)`, `LoadFailure.detail: Dictionary`, and `restore(data: Dictionary, ...)`. All of these sit in `src/kernel` or `src/shared`. ADR-0010 SIM-09 bans bare `Array` and undeclared bare `Dictionary` there, so the ADR's own interface listing fails the lint. If `blocks` becomes `Array[BlockDescriptor]`, every caller must pass a typed array. A bare literal is rejected for a typed-array parameter.
findings.amendment: Type the parameters: `blocks: Array[BlockDescriptor]` and `out_errors: Array[String]`, or a typed `BootError` record. Add `LoadFailure.detail` and the `restore` payload to the `dictionary_variant.json` allow-list, or reduce `detail` to a small typed record (reason, a, b). Tell the stories that callers build typed arrays.

findings.text: Packed arrays AND Array/Dictionary are reference types in GDScript. Probed on 4.7.2: after `block.col = payload["col"]`, a write to `block.col[0]` changed `payload["col"]`. An alias taken from a member also writes through to it, and a nested `Array` stored via `b.d = payload` aliases the payload. Section 3.1 phase 2 says `restore` "copies the contents into the existing block object" but does not require a deep copy. If a block assigns the staged columns by reference, then: (a) the live block aliases the payload that Save/Load or the single re-armed `SnapshotContext` put-slot still holds; (b) a default payload shared with a static or const default becomes mutable global state; (c) FixtureFactory `typical()` and `extreme()` results get mutated by the round trip, which can hide or fake idempotence failures. The same applies to `binding_source`: `ctx.put(PackedInt64Array)` hands the kernel a reference. If an owner returned a member array, the kernel would read live state, so it must be a fresh array per call (the ADR says 'derived per call'; make it a rule).
findings.amendment: Add to section 3.1 and the Implementation Guidelines: 'phase 2 copies by value. Packed columns are assigned from `.duplicate()` or rebuilt element by element, and nested Array/Dictionary are deep-copied. A block must never retain a reference to `data` or any of its members.' The kernel clears the `ctx.put` slot immediately after applying a `default_state` payload and before it re-arms the same context for `restore`. FixtureFactory methods return a fresh payload on every call. `binding_source` builds a new `PackedInt64Array` per call. Add one KRN-RST test: mutate the block after restore and assert that the payload bytes are unchanged.

findings.text: KRN-RST-10's leak guard (`OBJECT_COUNT`, `OBJECT_NODE_COUNT`, `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT`) only sees Object-derived leaks. P3 reproduces: 100 two-object RefCounted cycles gave a delta of 200 (the monitor returns float, `200.0`). Two other cycle types are not caught. 1,000 self-referencing Dictionary and Array pairs left OBJECT_COUNT at 0 and raised static memory by 612,192 bytes. A RefCounted that stores a lambda capturing `self` leaks one object per instance (delta 100 for 100 instances), so lambdas capturing `self` need a ban. Section 3.1's rule 'no reference cycle in scratch' and Verification 5 therefore claim more than the test can check. ADR-0010 already records this limit (P6, CNT-02).
findings.amendment: Extend KRN-RST-10 with the ADR-0010 CNT-02 `MEMORY_STATIC` tolerance check (debug and editor binaries only; release availability is UNVERIFIED there). Compare with `int()` casts, because `get_monitor` returns float. Add a lint or review rule: no self-referencing container in restore scratch, and no lambda or `Callable` capturing `self` stored in a RefCounted member. State that `OBJECT_COUNT` detects Object cycles only.

findings.text: P4 is true but vacuous. Headless, `RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED` reads `0.0` because the renderer is the dummy one (reproduced). A baseline `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` of 1 appeared even in a bare `--script` run, so cycle-1 versus cycle-n comparison must use deltas. 'Readable headless' does not mean 'measurable headless'. The node-count and render-texture legs that ADR-0028 adds cannot be validated in lane H. Whether `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` is populated in release exports is UNVERIFIED.
findings.amendment: Reword P4 to: 'the monitors return values headless but render monitors are 0 under the dummy renderer; render-texture legs run in the windowed lane W (ADR-0010 § 8)'. Specify KRN-RST-10 as a delta against cycle 1, not an absolute number. Mark the orphan monitor as debug-binary only.

findings.text: R1 check (a), 'every payload key names a registered block', does not say what order the payload keys are visited in. Dictionary iteration is insertion order, which is decoder order, so which unknown block gets named depends on the file's key order. Section 5.5 and KRN-RST-12 claim the first failure is a pure function of the payload, and section 2.2 says 'Dictionary iteration never decides anything'. Payload keys may also arrive as `String` where the registry holds `StringName`. ADR-0005 line 775 notes a Dictionary treats equal text as the same key, so lookup works, but ordering does not.
findings.amendment: Specify R1 as follows. Check (a) iterates the payload's keys converted to `String` and sorted by `BlockIdOrder`. Checks (b) to (d) iterate the registry in `RestorePlan.order`. Document that the first failure named is the first by that order.

findings.text: P1 is confirmed but the ADR understates it. `Array.sort()` and `<` on `StringName` are not lexical (reproduced on a 14-id set: `[layout, graph, sanity.perception, ... body]`). `Array[StringName].sort()` gives the identical wrong order. The result depends on interning order: the same four names created in the reverse order sorted alphabetically. That points to a pointer or intern-order compare, so it can differ between builds, platforms and hosts, not just between runs. The ADR says 'stable across two runs', which is the weaker framing, and ADR-0005 P12 already states it correctly. `StringName < StringName` also passes the analyzer (only mixed `StringName` against `String` is a parse error), so RST-01 must be type-aware and the compiler will not catch it. The `String(a) < String(b)` remedy is correct (code-point order, alphabetical in the probe). RST-01 overlaps the existing ADR-0005 AST rule 'StringName passed to sort()'.
findings.amendment: In P1 cite ADR-0005 P12 and say 'order depends on interning order; may differ between builds, platforms and hosts'. Make RST-01 a member of the ADR-0005 or DET lint rather than a parallel rule, with `<` and `>` added to its operand check. Note that KRN-RST-06 must pick ids whose interning order differs from alphabetical, including creating them in reverse order, because the bug is allocation-dependent.

findings.text: KRN-RST-05 uses a 'seeded shuffle of ready lists'. `Array.shuffle()` and `randi` use the global RNG, which is banned by DET-01 in sim and kernel. In the test tree it would make the order-permutation test non-reproducible or tied to global seeding. Separately, `RestorePlan` exposes its results as public `var order/rank/world_order/post_order/bind_order: PackedInt32Array`. They are reference types (see E3), so any holder can write through `plan.order[i] = x`. 4.7 element writes call no setter, so nothing intercepts it. The ADR calls the plan 'immutable'. The language has no readonly.
findings.amendment: Build the shuffled linear extensions with a test-owned Fisher-Yates driven by `DetRng` (ADR-0005), never `Array.shuffle()`. Make the plan fields private (`_order` and so on) and expose `order_at(i)`, `rank_of(index)` and `size()`. Or hand out `.duplicate()` copies and keep the immutability claim to 'immutable by convention, checked by hash of `describe()`'.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0017 D10.2 says registrants (Interaction, Horror, loot spawners, the actor boot) 're-register idempotently in their own `post_restore` (`restore_after` allows it)'. ADR-0016 section 4.2 forbids any `post_restore` from writing another block, and enforces it with a RESTORE-scope `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` refusal. V10 and section 4.3 move that repair into the owner's hook. This is a real conflict. It is not an engine problem, but it would turn into a refused write at runtime.
cross_adr.amendment: Amend ADR-0017 D10.2 to 'registrants re-register in their next ordinary hook run; `post_restore` only detects drift'. ADR-0016 section 4.2 already covers this, so only ADR-0017 and ADR-0020 need the sentence changed. Alternatively ADR-0016 may add an explicit exception, but that contradicts its own 'no cross-block write' table.

cross_adr.text: SIM-09 bans bare `Array` and undeclared bare `Dictionary` in `src/kernel`, `src/shared` and `src/sim`, which ADR-0016's own signatures violate (E2). RST-01 and the other proposed RST rules (RST-02 to RST-04) are a new pack. CNT-02 (`MEMORY_STATIC`) is the only existing guard for container cycles, and ADR-0016 KRN-RST-10 should use it (E4).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0010 should (a) add the `LoadFailure.detail` and `restore` payload entries to `dictionary_variant.json`, (b) accept the RST pack or fold RST-01 into DET/ADR-0005's StringName rule, and (c) cross-reference CNT-02 from KRN-RST-10.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0005 P12 already records that StringName order 'may change between runs and builds'. ADR-0016 P1 says 'stable across two runs' and calls the mechanism UNVERIFIED. toolu_01ByS8AuCAB43rauHkNJ9DNX.verdict: CONCERNS (engine): no blocking engine error. No API is deprecated, post-cutoff or mis-signed. The probed claims P1 and P3 reproduce on 4.7.2. Seven non-blocking amendments are needed before Acceptance. Three matter most: packed-array reference semantics at restore (E3), the blind spot in the KRN-RST-10 leak guard (E4), and one non-compiling Key Interfaces listing (E1).

findings.text: Key Interfaces puts `class_name LoadStage` and `class_name LoadFailure` under a single `# src/kernel/load_stage.gd` header. A GDScript file allows one `class_name`, so copying the block verbatim will not parse. The other listings (RestorePlan, BlockIdOrder, VerifyOut, FixtureFactory) each have a header and are fine. The `LoadStage` int constants are legal GDScript.
findings.amendment: Add a `# src/kernel/load_failure.gd` header above `class_name LoadFailure`. State that each listed class is its own file, as ADR-0003 does for fault classes.

findings.text: The Key Interfaces use bare `Array` and `Dictionary`: `RestorePlan.compile(blocks: Array, max_blocks: int, out_errors: Array)`, `LoadFailure.detail: Dictionary`, and `restore(data: Dictionary, ...)`. All of these sit in `src/kernel` or `src/shared`. ADR-0010 SIM-09 bans bare `Array` and undeclared bare `Dictionary` there, so the ADR's own interface listing fails the lint. If `blocks` becomes `Array[BlockDescriptor]`, every caller must pass a typed array. A bare literal is rejected for a typed-array parameter.
findings.amendment: Type the parameters: `blocks: Array[BlockDescriptor]` and `out_errors: Array[String]`, or a typed `BootError` record. Add `LoadFailure.detail` and the `restore` payload to the `dictionary_variant.json` allow-list, or reduce `detail` to a small typed record (reason, a, b). Tell the stories that callers build typed arrays.

findings.text: Packed arrays AND Array/Dictionary are reference types in GDScript. Probed on 4.7.2: after `block.col = payload["col"]`, a write to `block.col[0]` changed `payload["col"]`. An alias taken from a member also writes through to it, and a nested `Array` stored via `b.d = payload` aliases the payload. Section 3.1 phase 2 says `restore` "copies the contents into the existing block object" but does not require a deep copy. If a block assigns the staged columns by reference, then: (a) the live block aliases the payload that Save/Load or the single re-armed `SnapshotContext` put-slot still holds; (b) a default payload shared with a static or const default becomes mutable global state; (c) FixtureFactory `typical()` and `extreme()` results get mutated by the round trip, which can hide or fake idempotence failures. The same applies to `binding_source`: `ctx.put(PackedInt64Array)` hands the kernel a reference. If an owner returned a member array, the kernel would read live state, so it must be a fresh array per call (the ADR says 'derived per call'; make it a rule).
findings.amendment: Add to section 3.1 and the Implementation Guidelines: 'phase 2 copies by value. Packed columns are assigned from `.duplicate()` or rebuilt element by element, and nested Array/Dictionary are deep-copied. A block must never retain a reference to `data` or any of its members.' The kernel clears the `ctx.put` slot immediately after applying a `default_state` payload and before it re-arms the same context for `restore`. FixtureFactory methods return a fresh payload on every call. `binding_source` builds a new `PackedInt64Array` per call. Add one KRN-RST test: mutate the block after restore and assert that the payload bytes are unchanged.

findings.text: KRN-RST-10's leak guard (`OBJECT_COUNT`, `OBJECT_NODE_COUNT`, `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT`) only sees Object-derived leaks. P3 reproduces: 100 two-object RefCounted cycles gave a delta of 200 (the monitor returns float, `200.0`). Two other cycle types are not caught. 1,000 self-referencing Dictionary and Array pairs left OBJECT_COUNT at 0 and raised static memory by 612,192 bytes. A RefCounted that stores a lambda capturing `self` leaks one object per instance (delta 100 for 100 instances), so lambdas capturing `self` need a ban. Section 3.1's rule 'no reference cycle in scratch' and Verification 5 therefore claim more than the test can check. ADR-0010 already records this limit (P6, CNT-02).
findings.amendment: Extend KRN-RST-10 with the ADR-0010 CNT-02 `MEMORY_STATIC` tolerance check (debug and editor binaries only; release availability is UNVERIFIED there). Compare with `int()` casts, because `get_monitor` returns float. Add a lint or review rule: no self-referencing container in restore scratch, and no lambda or `Callable` capturing `self` stored in a RefCounted member. State that `OBJECT_COUNT` detects Object cycles only.

findings.text: P4 is true but vacuous. Headless, `RENDER_TEXTURE_MEM_USED` reads `0.0` because the renderer is the dummy one (reproduced). A baseline `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` of 1 appeared even in a bare `--script` run, so cycle-1 versus cycle-n comparison must use deltas. 'Readable headless' does not mean 'measurable headless'. The node-count and render-texture legs that ADR-0028 adds cannot be validated in lane H. Whether `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` is populated in release exports is UNVERIFIED.
findings.amendment: Reword P4 to: 'the monitors return values headless but render monitors are 0 under the dummy renderer; render-texture legs run in the windowed lane W (ADR-0010 § 8)'. Specify KRN-RST-10 as a delta against cycle 1, not an absolute number. Mark the orphan monitor as debug-binary only.

findings.text: R1 check (a), 'every payload key names a registered block', does not say what order the payload keys are visited in. Dictionary iteration is insertion order, which is decoder order, so which unknown block gets named depends on the file's key order. Section 5.5 and KRN-RST-12 claim the first failure is a pure function of the payload, and section 2.2 says 'Dictionary iteration never decides anything'. Payload keys may also arrive as `String` where the registry holds `StringName`. ADR-0005 line 775 notes a Dictionary treats equal text as the same key, so lookup works, but ordering does not.
findings.amendment: Specify R1 as follows. Check (a) iterates the payload's keys converted to `String` and sorted by `BlockIdOrder`. Checks (b) to (d) iterate the registry in `RestorePlan.order`. Document that the first failure named is the first by that order.

findings.text: P1 is confirmed but the ADR understates it. `Array.sort()` and `<` on `StringName` are not lexical (reproduced on a 14-id set: `[layout, graph, sanity.perception, ... body]`). `Array[StringName].sort()` gives the identical wrong order. The result depends on interning order: the same four names created in the reverse order sorted alphabetically. That points to a pointer or intern-order compare, so it can differ between builds, platforms and hosts, not just between runs. The ADR says 'stable across two runs', which is the weaker framing, and ADR-0005 P12 already states it correctly. `StringName < StringName` also passes the analyzer (only mixed `StringName` against `String` is a parse error), so RST-01 must be type-aware and the compiler will not catch it. The `String(a) < String(b)` remedy is correct (code-point order, alphabetical in the probe). RST-01 overlaps the existing ADR-0005 AST rule 'StringName passed to sort()'.
findings.amendment: In P1 cite ADR-0005 P12 and say 'order depends on interning order; may differ between builds, platforms and hosts'. Make RST-01 a member of the ADR-0005 or DET lint rather than a parallel rule, with `<` and `>` added to its operand check. Note that KRN-RST-06 must pick ids whose interning order differs from alphabetical, including creating them in reverse order, because the bug is allocation-dependent.

findings.text: KRN-RST-05 uses a 'seeded shuffle of ready lists'. `Array.shuffle()` and `randi` use the global RNG, which is banned by DET-01 in sim and kernel. In the test tree it would make the order-permutation test non-reproducible or tied to global seeding. Separately, `RestorePlan` exposes its results as public `var order/rank/world_order/post_order/bind_order: PackedInt32Array`. They are reference types (see E3), so any holder can write through `plan.order[i] = x`. 4.7 element writes call no setter, so nothing intercepts it. The ADR calls the plan 'immutable'. The language has no readonly.
findings.amendment: Build the shuffled linear extensions with a test-owned Fisher-Yates driven by `DetRng` (ADR-0005), never `Array.shuffle()`. Make the plan fields private (`_order` and so on) and expose `order_at(i)`, `rank_of(index)` and `size()`. Or hand out `.duplicate()` copies and keep the immutability claim to 'immutable by convention, checked by hash of `describe()`'.
